intro: Stand before Sarıhan Caravanserai, in Nevşehir province, built in 1249. Raised from Cappadocia's yellow stone, it is one of the last Seljuk hans on this branch of the Silk Road, its two-tone portal set against a deliberately plain courtyard.
history: Built in 1249, the han guarded the Kızılırmak crossing on the road from Aksaray to Kayseri, and it is among the last Seljuk caravanserais raised in Cappadocia. Its name comes from the yellow ashlar of the quarries around it. By the twentieth century it lay in ruins, but in the 1980s a thorough restoration raised it again.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal and the courtyard, then the kiosk mosque and the covered hall.
facts: Did you know? The two-tone stonework of the portal is deliberately set against the bare walls of the covered hall: the ornament is placed on the face the traveller sees from a distance. Sarıhan is among the latest of the Seljuk caravanserais in Cappadocia, and it takes its name from the yellow stone of the quarries around it. Close to collapse in the twentieth century, the building was raised again, whole, in the restoration of the 1980s.
outro: This brings our visit to Sarıhan Caravanserai to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Caravans once rested here on their long road; may your own journey go well. Enjoy your visit.
